title: Boston Travel Guide

hero.headline: Boston Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Plan a high-value Boston itinerary with top neighborhoods, outdoor access, and proven tour ideas.

overview: Boston is a strong base for culture, food, and outdoor day plans. Build each day around one anchor area, then add nearby experiences to reduce transit time.
For first-time visitors, pair iconic landmarks with one local neighborhood each day. This gives you a more complete feel for Boston without over-scheduling.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Harbor Islands
thingsToDo.description: Boston Harbor Islands National and State Park covers 34 islands and peninsulas in Boston Harbor and was formally designated as a National Recreation Area in 1996. Key stops include Georges Island and Civil War-era Fort Warren, with seasonal ferries from downtown Boston connecting visitors to beaches, trails, and harbor ecology sites.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Shoulder seasons are best for comfort and flexibility
bullets: Spring and fall typically offer the easiest weather for walking and tours.
Summer can be busy; reserve major attractions and timed entries early.
Winter trips can provide better rates and lighter midday crowds in many districts.

travelTips: Use early starts for major sights and popular viewpoints.
Pre-book top attractions and guided activities during peak months.
Keep one flexible block each day for weather or traffic changes.
Stay close to transit hubs if you want to minimize transfer time.

faq.q: How many days are ideal for Boston?
faq.a: Three to four days gives enough time for major attractions and one outdoor-focused day.

faq.q: Is Boston good for outdoor travelers?
faq.a: Yes. Most itineraries can combine city highlights with nearby hiking, water, or scenic touring options.

faq.q: Should I book tours in advance?
faq.a: For top-rated tours and peak travel weeks, advance booking is strongly recommended.
